target_customer: Travelers holding passports that require tourist visas, mainly Egyptian and Global South passport holders, paying per application
problem: Tourist visa applications involve heavy paperwork, document checks and scarce appointment slots for holders of weak passports.
business_model: Per-application service fees (itemized) with AI preparation, human expert review and optional appointment booking packages; also seeking distribution partners such as travel agencies

founders.name: Aly Moursy
previous_startups: Dlvvr (same-day delivery platform, co-founder, outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: Described by launch coverage as Canadian-Egyptian. YC page lists him as the only active founder.

competitors.name: Atlys
competitors.traction_then: reported about 700,000 applications a year in March 2026 (company-reported)

competitors.name: iVisa and HelloGov AI
competitors.what: AI-powered consumer passport and visa platform after merger

competitors.name: VisaHQ
competitors.what: Established visa and passport processing service, described as mostly form filling

technical_complexity.rationale: Document reading, form filling and WhatsApp workflows on top of existing models. Appointment booking against embassy and VFS systems and human review are operational work.

defensibility.rationale: Well funded incumbents like Atlys already offer AI-assisted visas and the workflow is easy to copy. Local distribution and trust in Egypt may help but are unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already offering AI-assisted visa applications when Veeza launched in October 2026. No outcome yet.

market_need_then: Large numbers of travelers from weak-passport countries need tourist visas, with documented friction in paperwork and appointments. Founder cites personal experience traveling on two passports.

branding.domain_note: Uses veeza.ai. Search results show confusion with unrelated names such as Veza and Veez AI.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, reassuring and transparent, for example a headline telling the user to name the destination and the company will apply; bilingual English and Arabic with WhatsApp as main contact

branding.brand_signature: AI does the work, a real person makes sure it is right

brand_strength.rationale: Launched only in October 2026 with some launch coverage; no evidence yet of community, merch or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Veeza AI is a Fall 2026 company that launched publicly on 2026-10-19 and was seeking distribution partners a day later. No outcome data exists yet. Its main challenge is that funded incumbents such as Atlys already sell AI-assisted visa applications, so its edge rests on founder insight into weak-passport travelers and local distribution in Egypt.
notes: Dealroom lists a roughly $500K seed round with investors hidden behind a paywall; single aggregator, unverified, so not recorded as a round. Competitor sources are 2026 pages dated near the batch. Founder education not found. Completeness pass: the roughly 500K USD seed is now recorded from Dealroom alone (date and investors hidden). Press searches found no announcement.
